surface_leak: After Huang, the bound is sqrt(n) while the cube carries n dimensions, which invites a further board change.
why_negative: Chung-Fueredi-Graham-Seymour's own construction gives a (2^{n-1}+1)-vertex induced subgraph with max degree ceil(sqrt n), so sqrt(n) is achieved and nothing further comes off. The matched positive is case 1, where the log DID come off.

tightness_scoped.what_is_tight: f(n), the minimum maximum-degree, equals ceil(sqrt n) for EVERY n. Integrality closes the rounding (Delta is an integer, so Delta >= sqrt n <=> Delta >= ceil(sqrt n)), and monotonicity (f(n) <= f(n+1), by splitting Q_{n+1}) makes CFGS's construction at perfect squares sufficient everywhere. Nothing further comes off THIS FUNCTIONAL.
tightness_scoped.what_is_NOT_closed: The sensitivity conjecture. Gotsman-Linial gives deg <= s^2 and IS tight; Nisan-Szegedy sharpened by Tal gives bs <= deg^2 and is NOT known tight (best separation bs = Omega(deg^1.63), Kushilevitz). Composite: bs <= s^4 against a best separation of (2/3)s^2 - s/3 (Ambainis-Sun), so the exponent is open in [2, 4], conjectured 2. The loss lives in the deg->bs step, which has nothing to do with the cube.
tightness_scoped.also_not_closed: The METHOD. The signing/interlacing argument has been generalised (Clifford-algebra reformulations, analogues for other regular and Cayley graphs, lambda_1 statements).
tightness_scoped.correction: An earlier version said 'nothing further comes off', conflating the extremal value with the sensitivity question. Scoped after the N9 audit.

diagnostic_status: OUT OF DOMAIN for product-law matching: the feasible set is not closed under the Cartesian product. The twin remains a valid NEGATIVE (the bound is tight), but it can no longer serve as a specificity test for this diagnostic.
